messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention exception follow-up: Acme Health

Hi John / Lisa

Great to meet you both earlier  thanks for the conversation and for walking through Acme Health's data handling requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Use case: real-time clinical note summarization from clinician input (PHI/PII sensitive)
- Primary requirement: no persistent storage of raw user inputs (0-retention for message content)
- Secondary asks: audit/logging for operational troubleshooting and SLA purposes, plus a signed BAA

Options we discussed (high level):
1) Zero-retention hosted: no conversation text stored after response is returned. Minimal ephemeral logs retained in-memory for processing.
2) Short retention: conversation data retained for a customer-configurable window (e.g., 7 days) with strict access controls and encryption at rest.
3) Private / on-prem: full control for customers requiring absolute data residency and audit separation.

Open questions for you:
- Is Acme comfortable with a short operational logs window (we typically retain request/response metadata for 7 days; full bodies only if enabled)?
- Do you have a timeline for a BAA? We can start with our standard draft and iterate.
- Any additional compliance artifacts we should send (SOC 2 summary, encryption spec)?

Next steps I propose:
- Camila to share a short options doc and a proposed minimal retention schedule for review (attached: short stub)
- Acme to confirm preference between 0-retention vs 7-day shortened logs
- If 0-retention is required, we will loop legal and engineering for a technical design & feasibility check

I've attached a one-page options summary for quick review. Happy to set a follow-up call early next week.

Thanks,
Camila
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: John Doe <john.doe@acmehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception follow-up: Acme Health

Hi Camila

Thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our compliance/legal side: 

- Acme Health is HIPAA-regulated. We need to ensure PHI is not persisted outside of our control. Preferably we want no persistent storage of message bodies.
- Audit logs (metadata only) are acceptable for troubleshooting, but we need to limit retention to no more than 14 days and redact PII from logs where possible.
- We will require a signed BAA prior to any production traffic.

I attached our high-level HIPAA_requirements.pdf for reference. Primary asks: 0-retention for conversation text, and if any short-term retention is needed for debugging, it must be configurable, encrypted, and retained no longer than 7 days.

Can you confirm Redwood's capability to implement a 0-retention configuration in the hosted product, or whether we would need a Private deployment? Also please include SOC 2 and encryption details.

Regards,
John
Director of IT Security | Acme Health
Attachment: HIPAA_requirements.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention exception follow-up: Acme Health

John

Thanks for the HIPAA requirements doc  that helps a lot. Short answers up front:

- We can support a 0-retention mode for conversation text in the hosted product for specific customers as an approved exception (this disables persistent storage of message bodies on our backend).
- Operational metadata (request id, timestamps, routing info, and token counts) are retained for diagnostics; by default we retain metadata for 30 days, but we can configure a shortened window (7 days) for customers with contractual requirements.
- We redact obvious PII from logs where feasible and encrypt all logs at rest (AES-256) with customer-specific KMS keys available on Dedicated/Private. For hosted exceptions we can document encryption-at-rest and access controls.

Technical notes / caveats:
- 0-retention disables storing of full request/response bodies, but some ephemeral in-memory state is required to execute inference. We will confirm retention boundaries with the infra team; for extreme cases we may recommend Private deployment (on-prem or VPC) if Acme needs absolute isolation.
- For debugging incidents we provide a controlled debug flow that requires an explicit ticket and time-limited temporary logging enabled by customer opt-in (we include full audit trail for any temporary enablement).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Redwood to propose contract language for a 0-retention hosted exception or a 7-day short-log alternative (we'll provide both options).
2) Camila/Aditya to provide SOC 2 summary and encryption spec doc (Aditya, can you attach the SOC 2 + encryption one-pager?)
3) John to confirm preference.

I'll draft the two contract language options this afternoon and loop legal. If acceptable, we can route the BAA and an addendum for 0-retention to DocuSign.

Best,
Camila

Camila

Nice summary. A couple of negotiation points to keep in mind when we propose contract language: 
- Offer the 7-day short-log option as the standard fallback; frame 0-retention as a limited exception that requires engineering sign-off and an addendum to the BAA.
- For 0-retention we should include explicit language on: (a) what "no persistent storage" means operationally, (b) the temporary debug enablement workflow and approval gates, and (c) proof points around encryption and access controls.
- Do not promise customer-managed KMS for hosted exceptions; that is an ask for Dedicated/Private. For hosted, offer customer-specific key scoping and strict RBAC on our side.

I'll draft suggested clauses for the addendum. Let's aim to send to Acme by EOD so John has something to review this week.

-Marissa
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
